newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Tajikistan to begin metallic antimony output.
newsitem.headline: Tajikistan to begin metallic antimony output.

text.p: The government of Tajikistan has commissioned a state factory to begin production of up to 500 tonnes of metallic antimony a year, mainly for sale to other former Soviet republics, Interfax news agency quoted the economy ministry as saying on Thursday.
Interfax said the state-owned Isfara plant would produce its first 20 tonnes of the metal in September and produce 250-300 tonnes in its first year.

The plant is trying to raise $1.5 million to improve output capacity to 2,000 tonnes per year. Over the last three years, Iskara was modernised for metallic antimony production at a cost of about $2 million, Interfax said.

Tajikistan has large antimony reserves but has previously sent antimony concentrate for final processing to the Kadamdzhaisky facility in Kyrgystan, which produces about 800 to 1,000 tonnes of antimony per month.
